story:
[emotion:QT/happy] Ethan ran toward the big wooden table in the school hall, where a massive toy train track stretched across three chairs. He had been thinking about building a rocket-train all morning, and the red engine was right there, waiting.

[emotion:QT/sad] But another boy, Ryan, was already reaching for the same red train. [emotion:QT/surprised] Both of them froze.

[emotion:QT/shy] "I thought I could use the red one," Ethan said quietly, while he held three curved track pieces in his hands.

[emotion:QT/calm] Ryan looked at Ethan carefully. "What if we build the track together? It'll be way longer than either of us could make alone.[gesture:think] [emotion:QT/calm] "

Ethan chewed his lip, then nodded slowly. Ryan gave Ethan the longer straight pieces, while Ethan snapped the curved sections around the chairs.

[emotion:QT/surprised] Suddenly, the track stretched all the way to the window. It was the longest rocket-train track either of them had ever seen.

[gesture:hoora] [emotion:QT/happy] Ryan cheered loudly, and Ethan laughed so hard his whole chest shook. After they ran the red train through every loop, Ryan said, "Same time Thursday?[gesture:nodding-yes] [emotion:QT/happy] " Ethan grinned. "Yeah. Definitely Thursday."

paragraphs: Ethan ran toward the big wooden table in the school hall, where a massive toy train track stretched across three chairs. He had been thinking about building a rocket-train all morning, and the red engine was right there, waiting.
But another boy, Ryan, was already reaching for the same red train. Both of them froze.
"I thought I could use the red one," Ethan said quietly, while he held three curved track pieces in his hands.
Ryan looked at Ethan carefully. "What if we build the track together? It'll be way longer than either of us could make alone."
Ethan chewed his lip, then nodded slowly. Ryan gave Ethan the longer straight pieces, while Ethan snapped the curved sections around the chairs.
Suddenly, the track stretched all the way to the window. It was the longest rocket-train track either of them had ever seen.
Ryan cheered loudly, and Ethan laughed so hard his whole chest shook. After they ran the red train through every loop, Ryan said, "Same time Thursday?" Ethan grinned. "Yeah. Definitely Thursday."

questions.question: What is the main message Ethan learned while he was building the train track with Ryan?
wrong_answers: Red trains are the fastest vehicles.
It is best to play alone.

questions.question: What kind of special vehicle was Ethan thinking about building with the red engine before Ryan arrived?
After Ethan and Ryan worked together, where did their really long train track stretch all the way to?
How do you think Ethan felt when Ryan suggested they build the track together, and why did he chew his lip?
questions.correct_answer: He was thoughtful and surprised, because he was deciding if it was a good idea.
wrong_answers: He felt angry, because he wanted to play alone.
He was very happy, because he loved Ryan's idea right away.

questions.question: If Ethan and Ryan had not decided to share the red train, what do you think would have happened with their train track?
questions.correct_answer: It would have been much shorter than the one they built.
wrong_answers: They would have built two very long tracks by themselves.
A game hero would have come to help them build it.

questions.question: What is one lesson from this story about sharing?
questions.correct_answer: Sharing something you want makes the fun bigger for everyone.
wrong_answers: It's important to always get what you want first.
Playing by yourself means you don't have to compromise.

questions.question: What did Ethan and Ryan show us by building the track together?
questions.correct_answer: Working together with a friend helps you do more than you could alone.
wrong_answers: It's good to have a plan before you start playing.
Sometimes it's better to let someone else take the lead.

questions.question: What can you learn from how Ethan and Ryan became friends?
questions.correct_answer: Being brave enough to talk to someone new is how friendships start.
wrong_answers: It's always best to wait for someone else to speak first.
You should only play with people you already know well.

takeaways: Sharing something you want makes the fun bigger for everyone.
Working together with a friend helps you do more than you could alone.
Being brave enough to talk to someone new is how friendships start.
